correctness.rationale: A support partition of every Italian function is unique and the five allowed states for positive roots, two for boundary-zero roots and one for interior-zero roots are exhaustive and sufficient. They give the polynomial summand exactly. The equality max b_G(P)=n-gamma(G) follows from a sharp dominating-set inequality and attainment, giving the leading coefficient as sum 2^|P|. The C++ standalone direct checker exhausts all 1099 labeled simple graphs with 1 to 5 vertices and checks 22719 coefficient positions; an independent Python checker corroborates orders up to four and four five-vertex families. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed new result is the coefficientwise all-weight transform for every one-leaf corona of any finite simple base, not the scalar minimum value. The 2017 Roman-two Theorem 3.2 covers the scalar value exactly; the 2026 sunlet theorem covers optimum multiplicities for cycle bases; the inspected restrained-Italian and pointwise-minimal-Roman corona theorems enumerate different classes. None of the searched and materially inspected relevant theorems states or implies the unrestricted universal polynomial. Historical priority is provisional owing to potentially unindexed exact weight formulas.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier all-weight corona formula or general generating-function identity could cover the result; searched sources cannot prove global uniqueness.
Subset-boundary transforms for several related domination variants exist and should be examined in subsequent independent priority review.
No independent expert audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The all-weight Italian domination polynomial is a natural recently studied graph invariant, and the theorem gives a complete exact classification over every finite simple base graph rather than a selected narrow instance. The boundary transform counts every weight, extends beyond known scalar optimization and cycle-corona minimum counts, and yields an explicit general optimizer-multiplicity formula. Exponential subset summation and unproven computational complexity are disclosed; a polynomial-time or downstream breakthrough is not necessary to its structural enumerative value.
